He did not say "two signs" (آيَتَيْنِ) as He said, ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾ [al-Isra: 12], because their condition together is one sign, namely her giving birth to him without a male (fahl). Or the implied meaning is: "We made her a sign and her son likewise a sign", so آيَةً (āyatan, "a sign") is the object of the conjoined element (ma'tuf 'alayh, the word to which another is joined). What indicates this is the recitation (qira'a, a canonical variant reading) of those who read آيَتَيْنِ (āyatayn, "two signs").

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 92:

﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾. Al-ummah: the millah (religious community, creed). "This" is a pointer to the millat al-Islam (the religion of Islam), which is the millah of all the prophets. "One community" is a circumstantial state (hal): meaning united, not divided. The operative element (al-'amil) is what the demonstrative pronoun indicates, i.e., that the religion of Islam is your millah, which you must adhere to and not deviate from. It is pointed to as one millah, not differing. ﴿And I am your Lord, so worship Me﴾. That is: I have nurtured you by choice, so worship Me in gratitude and in pride. The address is to all of mankind.

﴿And they divided their affair among themselves﴾. The original wording was "and you (pl.) divided," but the speech was turned to the third person (ghaybah) by way of *iltifat* (a shift in grammatical person). The meaning: they made the matter of their religion into pieces among themselves, becoming sects and factions. Then He warned them that these divided groups, ﴿all of them will return to Us﴾, so We will recompense them for their deeds. (p-٤٢٠)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 94:

﴿Whoever does righteous deeds﴾ of any kind ﴿while he is a believer﴾ in what belief in it is obligatory ﴿his effort will not be denied﴾. That is: his effort is appreciated and accepted. ﴿Kufran﴾ (denial, ingratitude) is a metaphor for the deprivation of reward, just as ﴿shukr﴾ (gratitude, appreciation) is a metaphor for its bestowal. It has been negated with the negation of the genus (nafy al-jins, the negation of the whole category) so that it would be more emphatic (ablagh). ﴿And indeed We are for it﴾, that is, for the effort, ﴿recorders﴾ (katibun), that is, the guardian angels by Our command, ﴿in the record of his deeds﴾, so We reward him for it.

{And prohibited} — "wa-ḥirmun" is read by the Kufans, except Ḥafs, and Khalaf; the two are dialectal variants, like ḥill and ḥalāl in pattern, and their meaning is opposite. By ḥarām is meant "that whose existence is impossible." ﴿Upon a town which We have destroyed — that they will not return.﴾ The meaning: it is impossible, and not possible, for a people destroyed not to return to Allah by resurrection. Or: ﴿And prohibited upon a town which We have destroyed﴾ means: We decreed their destruction, or We judged that they be destroyed, namely that which is mentioned in the preceding verse, of righteous deeds and thankworthy striving that is not ungrateful. ﴿That they will not return﴾ from disbelief to Islam.

“Until” (ḥattā) is the particle after which speech is related, and the related speech is the sentence of condition and consequence, namely “when” (idhā) and what falls within its scope: ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose﴾, i.e., their barrier is opened, so the genitive (al-muḍāf, “their barrier”) is omitted, just as the genitive is omitted in “a town” (qarya) in the reading “were opened” (futtiḥat), transmitted by Ibn ʿĀmir (Shāmī). They are two tribes of the kind of mankind; it is said that mankind is ten parts, nine of which are Gog and Magog. ﴿And they﴾ refers to the people driven to the place of gathering (al-maḥshar); and it is said they are Gog and Magog, who come out when the barrier is opened. ﴿From every hill﴾, i.e., every elevated rise of the earth, ﴿they will swarm﴾, i.e., they will hasten.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 97:

﴿And the true promise draws near﴾, that is, the Resurrection (al-qiyamah). The answer (jawab) of "idha" (when) is ﴿then, behold﴾, and "idha" here is the sudden-surprise "idha" (idha al-mufajaah), which occurs in conditional sentences in place of the "fa" (then), as in His saying ﴿when they despair﴾ [al-Rum: 36]. When the "fa" comes with it, the two cooperate in connecting the response to the condition, so it is reinforced. Were one to say "fa-hiya shakhisatun" (then it is fixed) or "idha hiya shakhisatun", it would be sound. (p-421) And "hiya" is an ambiguous pronoun (damir mubham) which is clarified by "al-absar" (the eyes) and explained by ﴿the eyes of those who disbelieved are fixed, staring﴾, that is, their eyelids are raised and they hardly blink, from the terror of what they are in. ﴿They say: Woe to us!﴾ is connected to an omitted verb whose estimated form is: they say "Woe to us!", and "yaquluna" (they say) is a circumstantial clause (hal) from ﴿those who disbelieved﴾. ﴿We were indeed heedless of this﴾ [that is, this day], ﴿nay, we were wrongdoers﴾ by placing worship in other than its proper place.

You (all) and what you worship besides Allah (﴿إنَّكم وما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللهِ﴾): he means the idols and Iblis and his helpers, because by their obedience to them and their following of their footsteps, they are in the position of their worshippers. ﴿Fuel (ḥaṣab)﴾: firewood. It is also read ḥaṭab (with ṭa' instead of ṣad), ﴿of Hell; you are going to it as bound-for (wāridūn)﴾: entering into it.

﴿If these were gods,﴾ as you claimed, ﴿they would not have entered it.﴾ They would not have entered the Fire. ﴿And all of them,﴾ that is, the worshipper and the worshipped, ﴿in it,﴾ in the Fire, ﴿will abide forever.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 100:

﴿For them﴾ (i.e., for the disbelievers) ﴿therein is a zafir﴾, meaning moaning, weeping and wailing. ﴿And they therein do not hear﴾ anything, because they have become deaf, and hearing carries a kind of comfort (uns), so they were not given it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 101:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (al-husna) has preceded from Us﴾ The preferred quality in goodness is the feminine form of the superlative "al-ahsan" (the best). It is happiness, or the glad tidings of reward, or being granted success in obedience.

It was revealed in reply to the words of Ibn al-Za'bara when the Prophet (ﷺ) recited to the chieftains of Quraysh: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98] up to His words ﴿will abide﴾ [al-Anbiya: 102]. He said: "Did not the Jews worship 'Uzayr, the Christians the Messiah, and the sons of Mulayh the angels?" On the basis that His words "and what you worship" include them. For "ma" (what) is used for those who do not reason, but they were people of obstinacy, so the explanation was extended (p-422) with ﴿those﴾, meaning 'Uzayr, the Messiah and the angels, ﴿from it﴾, from Hell, ﴿will be kept far away﴾, because they did not approve of being worshipped.

It has also been said that the intended meaning of His words ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ is all the believers, based on what is related: that 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) recited this verse and then said: "I am among them, and Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, Talha, al-Zubayr, Sa'd and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf." Al-Junayd (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "The care (al-'inaya) preceded for them from Us at the beginning, so guardianship (al-wilaya) appeared for them at the end."

﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾: its sound that is perceived, and the movement of its blazing. This is an exaggeration regarding distancing from it, meaning: they will not come near it, so that they do not even hear its sound or the sound of those within it. ﴿And they, in what their souls desire﴾ of bounty, ﴿will abide eternally﴾, remaining. Desire (shahwa) is the soul's seeking of pleasure.

﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾: the final blast (al-nafkha al-akhira). ﴿And the angels will meet them﴾, meaning the angels will receive them, congratulating them at the gates of Paradise, saying: ﴿This is your day which you were promised﴾, meaning: this is the time of your reward, which your Lord promised you in the world.

The governing element of ﴿the day We roll up the heaven﴾ is ﴿does not grieve them﴾, or it is ﴿they will be met﴾. "The heaven is rolled up" is read by Yazid. Its rolling up means the stars being folded up and their traces erased, or it is the opposite of spreading out: ﴿We gather it and roll it up﴾. ﴿Like the rolling of the scroll﴾, that is, the written sheet, ﴿for the books﴾. Hamza, ʿAli and Hafs read "lil-kutub" (for the written things), meaning for the many meanings written in it. The others read "lil-kitab" (for the writing), meaning as the scroll is rolled up for writing, that is, for what is written in it, because "al-kitab" originally is a verbal noun, like "al-binaʾ," and then it is applied to the thing written. It was also said that "al-sijill" is an angel who rolls up the books of the children of Adam when they are raised to him. It was also said that it is a scribe who belonged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). On this view, "al-kitab" is the name of the written sheet, and the rolling (al-tayy) is attributed to the agent. On the first view, it is attributed to the object. ﴿As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it﴾.

The kaf (ك) in ﴿kama﴾ is in the accusative by an implied verb, which is explained by "nuʿiduhu" (We shall repeat it). "Ma" is a relative pronoun (mawsula), meaning: We shall repeat it like the one We began; "nuʿiduhu" is the repetition. "Awwala khalqin" is an adverb of time (ẓarf) governed by "badaʾna" (We began), meaning: the first thing that was created. Or it is a circumstantial accusative (ḥal) from the dropped pronoun of the relative clause, which is present in meaning though absent from the wording. The sense is: the first of the creation is its bringing into being. So as He brought it into being first, He repeats it a second time, likening the repetition to the initiation, since power applies equally to both. The indefiniteness of "khalq" is like your saying: "He is the first man who came to me," meaning the first of the men. But you made it singular and indefinite, intending to distinguish them one man at a time. Likewise, the meaning of ﴿awwala khalq﴾ is "the first of the creation," in the sense of "the first of the creatures," because "khalq" is a verbal noun which is not pluralized. ﴿waʿdan﴾ is an emphatic verbal noun (maṣdar muʾakkid), because His saying "nuʿiduhu" is a promise of the repetition. ﴿ʿalayna﴾ means: a promise that must certainly come to pass. ﴿Indeed We are ever doers﴾ of that, that is, those who certainly fulfil this promise. So prepare for it, and send ahead righteous deeds to be saved from these terrors.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 105:

﴿And We certainly wrote in the Zabur﴾ (the Psalms), the Book of Dawud (peace be upon him), ﴿after the Reminder﴾ (the Tawrat, the Torah), ﴿that the earth﴾ (i.e., al-Sham, the Levant), ﴿shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾. The letter ya' in ﴿ʿibādiya﴾ is read with sukun (silent) by Hamzah; others read it with fatha on the ya'. ﴿The righteous﴾, i.e., the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). Or, al-Zabur is in the sense of al-mazbur, i.e., the written, meaning: what was sent down to the prophets of the books. And "al-Dhikr" is Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book), meaning al-Lawh (the Preserved Tablet), because all of them took from it. The evidence for this is the reading of Hamzah and Khalaf with a damma on the zay, as the plural of zubur in the sense of mazbur. And "the earth" is the earth of Paradise.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 106:

﴿Indeed, in this﴾ — that is, the Qur'an, or what is mentioned in this surah of reports, promise, warning and admonitions — ﴿is surely a message﴾ — sufficiency (kifaya). Its origin is what one attains by it the desired goal (al-bughya) — ﴿for a people who worship﴾ — who affirm the oneness of God (muwahhidin), and they are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

We have not sent you except as a mercy ﴿وَما أرْسَلْناكَ إلا رَحْمَةً﴾ to the worlds. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am only a mercy bestowed" (إنَّما أنا رَحْمَةٌ مُهْداةٌ). ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾, because he brought what makes them happy if they follow him. As for whoever does not follow him, he has only brought it upon himself (مِن عِنْدِ (p-٤٢٤) نَفْسِهِ), since he has squandered his share of it. It was also said that he is a mercy to the believers in both abodes, and to the disbelievers in this world, by delaying the punishment of uprooting (الِاسْتِئْصال, istisal: total annihilation), transformation (المَسْخ, maskh: being changed into another form), and sinking into the earth (الخَسْف, khasf: being swallowed by the earth).

The word رَحْمَةً is a maf'ul li-hi (مَفْعُولٌ لَهُ, object of purpose, indicating the reason for the action), or it is a ḥāl (حالٌ, circumstantial accusative), meaning: "in a state of being a mercy" (أيْ: ذا رَحْمَةٍ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 108:

﴿Say, "It is only﴾ "innama" (inna-ma) is used to restrict a judgment to a thing, or to restrict a thing to a judgment, such as "innama Zaydun qa'imun" (Zayd is only standing) and "innama yaqumu Zaydun" (only Zayd stands). The agent (fa'il) of ﴿is revealed to me﴾ is "annama ilahukum ilahun wahid" (that your God is one God). The estimate (taqdir) is: "yuha ila ya wahdaniyyatu ilahi" (the oneness of my God is revealed to me). It is also permissible that the meaning be: "anna alladhi yuha ilayya" (that which is revealed to me), in which case "ma" is a relative pronoun (mawsula). ﴿So will you submit?﴾ is an interrogative used in the sense of a command, meaning: "aslimu" (submit!).

"If they turn away" from Islam, "then say: I have informed you" (ءاذنتكم), that is, I have made known to you what I was commanded, "on equal terms" (على سواء). This is a circumstantial clause (حال), meaning: you are equal in being informed of it, and I have not singled out some of you [over others]. In this is evidence of the falsity of the doctrine of the Batiniyya (al-Batiniyya, the esoteric sect).

"And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far." That is: I do not know when the Day of Resurrection will occur, because God Most High has not informed me of it, but I know that it is certainly going to happen without doubt. And I do not know when the punishment will descend upon you if you do not believe.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 110:

﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud, and He knows what you conceal.﴾ That is: He is Knowing of everything. He knows what you openly direct at me of defamation of Islam, and what you conceal in your breasts of resentment toward the Muslims, and He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 111:

﴿And I do not know: perhaps it is a trial for you﴾. And I do not know that the delay of the punishment for you in this world is a test for you, so that He may see how you act. ﴿And an enjoyment for a time﴾, and a granting of respite to you until death, so that this may be a proof against you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 112:

﴿He said: "My Lord, judge with truth."﴾ Decide between us and the people of Makkah with justice, or with the punishment that is due for them, and do not show them leniency, and be severe upon them, as He said: "O Allah, make your tread heavy upon Mudar" (ﷺ). "He said: 'My Lord'" — Hafs reads it as a quotation of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "My Lord is most judging" (Yazid, from Ya'qub). ﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful﴾, who is kind to His creation. ﴿The One whose help is sought﴾, the One from whom aid is requested. ﴿Against what you describe﴾. And from Ibn Dhakwan, with the ya' (yasifun, "they describe"): they used to describe the situation contrary to how it had actually turned out, and they hoped that power and victory would be theirs. So Allah refuted their assumptions and frustrated their hopes, and gave victory to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, and humiliated them, i.e., the disbelievers. And He is the One whose help is sought against what they describe.
